key_insight: A speech-based multimodal LLM approach that combines audio and transcript embeddings can improve cognitive impairment detection and generalize better across datasets.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a non-invasive screening framework that could support earlier identification of cognitive impairment using routinely collected speech data.
method: Extract acoustic embeddings from speech audio.
Generate textual embeddings from automatic transcripts.
Concatenate modality-specific features for downstream classification with open-source LLMs.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on ADReSS20 and ADReSSo21, the model achieved 92.4% accuracy and outperformed single-modality baselines with strong cross-dataset generalization.
watch_item: Performance depends on transcript quality and recording conditions, so real-world deployment may face robustness and privacy/implementation challenges.
paper_title: Toward Generalizable Cognitive Impairment Detection with Speech-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
